text:
jamie: Heads-up: found another awkwardness with AsyncClient.tool.call + structured_output + typing. Repro is tiny and affects mypy users.

lee: can you paste the snippet?

jamie: sure:
```py
from typing import TypedDict
from redwood import AsyncClient

class Order(TypedDict):
    id: str
    quantity: int

client = AsyncClient()

async def get_order(text: str) -> Order:
    res = await client.tool.call("parse_order", {"text": text}, output_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {"id": {"type": "string"}, "quantity": {"type": "integer"}}})
    return res  # mypy complains: Incompatible return type "dict[str, Any]"; expected "Order"
```

jamie: runtime returns a dict shaped like Order, but stubs show ToolCallResult as ``dict[str, Any]`` for awaitable variant. So typing parity is missing between sync and async APIs.

lee: that explains the lint noise we've been seeing. I think our stub generator emits ToolResult[T] for sync but AsyncToolResult is unparametrized. 

ron: FWIW I hit this too — and the auto-conversion/coercion step is inconsistent between tool.run and tool.call in async path (numbers as strings sometimes). The typing mismatch makes it hard to provide a clean wrapper.

jamie: workaround for now: cast on return `return res  # type: ignore[return-value]` or `cast(Order, res)` which is noisy.

lee: proposed fix: 1) make async Tool.call/Tool.run return Awaitable[T] in .pyi stubs (so mypy infers Order), 2) ensure post-processing coercion runs before typing boundary (so users get ints not strings), 3) add integration sample in samples/python/typed-toolcall-async demonstrating TypedDict end-to-end.

jamie: also request: can we add a short "mypy notes" doc fragment to sdk/README about current typing caveats + recommended patterns until stubs are fixed? Saved me time.

devx-bot: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2401 "async tool.call missing generic return type in stubs; inconsistent coercion" (labels: devex, p2).

ron: I'll pick up the stub change. @lee can you handle the coercion pipeline change?

lee: yep. I'll add unit tests & a small e2e that runs against the local harness. Also plan to add a MyPy check in CI to prevent regressions.

jamie: awesome. One more small thing: sample output in docs should show TypedDict example and the minimal server mock to reproduce. That helped me debug quickly.

lee: agreed. I'll author the sample and link it in the issue.

jamie: thanks all :rocket:
